header:
Question 9 The Appeal of Self-Immolative Reactions
Fragmentation is an important and elegant class of skeletal-reorganization processes in organic chemistry. Classical fragmentations are usually controlled by specific electronic effects and cleave otherwise inert chemical bonds through concerted electron transfer.

subquestions.text_open: 9.1 Write the SMILES strings for at least 2 key intermediates in the following Eschenmoser–Tanabe fragmentation.

text_images.description: The figure shows the one-step sequence 'CC1CC2(OC2C(C1)=O)C'>1. TsNHNH2, rt; 2. 55°C, 2h, 50%>'CC(CC(CC#C)C)=O'.

subquestions.text_open:
In recent years, chemists have introduced the concept of fragmentation driven by a cascade of electron transfers into drug delivery and smart sensing, developing self-immolative reactions. Such systems usually consist of a trigger group, a conjugated linker, and a leaving payload. When a specific stimulus activates the trigger, long-range concerted fragmentation begins within the molecule, causing spontaneous disassembly and release of the target molecule.
9.2 In the following molecule, reduction serves as the specific stimulus. After neutral intermediate A forms, self-immolation occurs immediately. Write the SMILES string for intermediate A.

The reaction produces 2 inorganic and 2 organic products. Write the SMILES strings for the 2 organic products and the formulas of the 2 inorganic products.

9.4 Ring formation is fundamental to organic reactions. Certain ring-forming reactions can also serve as specific stimuli that initiate self-immolation.
9.4.1 In the reaction above, the substrate undergoes Michael addition to give B. Self-immolation of B forms seven-membered-ring compound C. Write the SMILES string for C and the chemical formula of the small inorganic molecule produced.

text_images.description: The figure shows the one-step reaction 'C=CC(OC1=CC=C(COC(NC2=CC=CC=C2)=S)C=C1)=O'.'SC[C@H](N)C(O)=O'>PBS (PH=7.4, 10mM)>[B]. The cysteine thiol is shown with a dashed wedge to indicate stereochemistry, retained by the @ marker in the SMILES. The product is labeled only B and its structure is not shown.

subquestions.text_open: 9.4.2 Ring formation is not the endpoint; a pericyclic reaction follows. This strategy uses the inverse-electron-demand Diels–Alder reaction (IEDDA) between a trans-cyclooctene derivative (TCO) and a tetrazine derivative to trigger self-immolation. In the reaction below, IEDDA between TCO and tetrazine releases a gas and forms a dihydropyridazine intermediate. After the pericyclic reaction, an N atom of the dihydropyridazine acts as the initiating group for self-immolation, producing 2 aromatic organic compounds. Write the SMILES strings for both products.

text_images.description: The figure shows the one-step reaction 'CC1=NN=C(C)N=N1'.'O=C(NC1=CC=CC=C1)OC2CCCCC/C=C/2'>>[products not shown].

subquestions.text_open: 9.4.3 The dihydropyridazine intermediate must undergo a formal σ-migration rearrangement before it can initiate 1,4-elimination, the subsequent self-immolation. Name this rearrangement and explain why it is faster in water than in an organic phase.

9.5 The following substance can undergo a self-immolative reaction through rearrangement.
Write the SMILES strings for 1 key rearrangement intermediate containing 2 five-membered rings and the 2 organic molecules produced by self-immolation.
